# QUESTIONs with `line` `record-as-apparatus`

*Lines of inquiry — A named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found. Retracting a line is a status change on its members, never a deletion (ADR-032).*

| [QUESTION-366](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-366.md) v2 | Does an inquiry need the record of its own development to know its object, as Simondon's method and its organization-studies readers hold, or only to revise its conclusions, which is what the record has shown? | Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024, p. 1366), quoting Simondon, hold that research "consists in following the being in its genesis, in accomplishing the genesis of thought at the same time as the genesis of the object", and Bencherki and Iliadis (proposition 4) that knowledge of an entity "should reflect on the way that knowledge itself has individuated". The record has shown a narrower thing: an inquiry's history is needed to fix its revisions ([CLAIM-294](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-294.md)), and a stabilized specification lets later inquiry proceed without repeating the history that made it ([CLAIM-475](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-475.md)). Whether the history is needed for anything besides revision is open, and an answer would also say whether the record's objects are constituted by its inquiry in any sense beyond [CLAIM-469](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-469.md)'s operational one, which is [CLAIM-476](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-476.md)'s unanswered defeater. | Open |
